review_notes: I read the whole file. Its only definition is `CommGroup.toDistribLattice`, a constructor for a distributive lattice. I grepped Mathlib for other `toDistribLattice` definitions and for other lattice-ordered-group distributivity constructions. The other hits were Frame, Heyting and Boolean algebra instances, which are different concepts. `Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Group/Unbundled/Abs.lean` uses this definition, so it doesn't compete with it. The lemmas `mul_sup`, `sup_mul`, `inv_sup`, `sup_div` and the rest are group-specific. They share names only with ideal, submodule and NNReal lemmas that live in other namespaces and state different things. The lemmas are already proved through `OrderIso.mulLeft`, `OrderIso.mulRight`, `OrderIso.inv` and `OrderIso.divLeft`, so they don't re-implement existing infrastructure. Standalone lemma duplication is outside this rubric. I found no avoidable competing version of an existing concept.
